title: Brauer pullback to the reduction of a curve
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $f:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ a separated finite-type scheme of dimension at most one (a curve [def-sc-curves], without the algebraic-closedness restriction). Let $i:C_{\mathrm{red}}\to C$ be its reduction [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. The canonical pullback
$$H^2(C_{\mathrm{Et}},\mathbf G_{m,C})\longrightarrow H^2((C_{\mathrm{red}})_{\mathrm{Et}},\mathbf G_{m,C_{\mathrm{red}}})$$
is injective. Here cohomology is [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] and the groups are cohomological Brauer groups [def-br]. The map is the cohomology pullback to $i^*\mathbf G_{m,C}$ followed by the map induced by $i^*\mathbf G_{m,C}\to\mathbf G_{m,C_{\mathrm{red}}}$. Neither smoothness, properness nor reducedness of $C$ is assumed.

proof.text: The reduction is a surjective closed immersion. Typeclass inference uses that closed immersions are finite, hence integral, and universally injective to construct IsUniversalHomeomorphism. Topological invariance makes cohomologyMap i G_m 2 bijective.
The units comparison varphi on C_red is epi. Form the canonical kernel short exact sequence ker(varphi) -> i^{-1}G_m,C -> G_m,C_red.

The H^2 of ker(varphi) vanishes. Exactness of H^2(kernel) -> H^2(i^{-1}G_m) -> H^2(G_m,C_red) says every element in the kernel of the latter map is the image of an element in a zero group. It is therefore zero, giving injectivity.
Compose this injective map with the injective cohomologyMap. Their composite is definitionally the canonical pullback in the unchanged statement.
